images.prompt: The garden at sunset. The place is the small, quiet back garden of an old Japanese house in the Meiji era, seen from the low veranda. Soft, thick green moss covers the ground. Just right of centre in the middle distance, on the moss, lies one smooth, round, weathered grave stone, about the size of a large cushion, a little rounded like a pebble polished by falling a long way through the sky, with patches of moss on its shoulders. Resting on the moss in front of the stone is one large opened pearl shell (a big smooth sea shell with a nacreous, iridescent inner surface), lying hollow side up. Behind them, a low old earthen garden wall with a small tiled coping runs across the frame, and beyond the wall the dark rounded tops of a few old pine and camphor trees. Above the wall a wide, open sky fills the upper half of the image. The stone and the shell are the only objects in the garden: no lanterns, no stone lanterns, no torii, no shrines, no temples, no gates, no bridges, no fences, no steps, no water basins, no ponds, no streams, no boats, no people, no figures, no hands, no animals, no birds, no insects, no cats. No cherry blossoms, no plum blossoms, no maple leaves, no autumn colours, no bamboo, no pampas grass, no susuki, no snow, no rice paddies. Keep the round grave stone, the pearl shell, the moss, the earthen wall, the trees and the viewpoint exactly as in the reference scene 03: same positions, same sizes, same outlines. Change only the sky, the light and the atmosphere. A large, round, deep red setting sun hangs low in the sky above the wall, left of centre, partly touching the dark tree tops; the sky is a soft gradated wash from deep vermilion and warm orange low down to dusky rose and pale violet above. The round stone and the moss catch the last warm red light on their edges, and the inside of the pearl shell glows faintly pink. No moon, no stars. Vermilion, warm orange, dusky rose, soft moss green, warm grey stone. This is the brightest scene.
